_source: Places whose point is chosen by hand (pipeline/build_data.py, move_points and pick_site). `same_as`: the place sits on another OpenBible record's point. OpenBible calls each of these 'another name for' the other record, but resolves the two one hop apart, to different candidate sites (docs/crosswalk/their-errors.md, O6): one place, one point; a chain (Bealoth -> Baalath-beer -> Ramah 6) is followed to its end. `site`: one of OpenBible's modern locations for the place, shown in place of its first identification, with its point, its confidence and its 'where it is today' line; the candidates on the card are unchanged. Chosen where the majority of the atlases and reference works (Pleiades and the Barrington Atlas, Wikidata, OpenBible's count of sources) holds another candidate than OpenBible's recent-trend weighting (docs/crosswalk/their-errors.md, the last section, 'decided by the majority on 2026-10-19'). Checked by hand on 2026-10-19; Zer (a061538) was taken out again the same day on review: the named record's own point fits its verses worse (O6).

ac17675.why: Dimonah (Josh 15:22) is Dibon of Judah (Neh 11:25), in the Negeb list of Josh 15:21-32; OpenBible's resolution lands on Dibon of Moab, 63 km away.

a92de65.why: Bethul (Josh 19:4): another name for Bethuel, which sits with Bethel 2 at Khirbet el-Qaryatein; resolved to Bethuel's second candidate, 23 km west.

acf2fac.why: Chesil (Josh 15:30): another name for Bethuel; the same resolution as Bethul.

ae83efa.why: Canneh (Ezek 27:23): another name for Calneh 2, resolved 74 km from it.

a6c0a5f.why: Ir-moab (Num 22:36): another name for Ar, resolved 9 km from it.

ad259d1.why: Sea of Jazer (Jer 48:32): another name for Jazer, resolved 11 km from it.

a5c4318.why: Hukok (1 Chr 6:75): another name for Helkath, resolved 8 km from it.

a901903.why: Hukkok (Josh 19:34): Yaquq (Huqoq), where the name survives, is the identification of most reference works (OpenBible: 15 sources to 12, 202 votes to 174) and of Wikidata Q18608506, which our record links; Khirbet el-Jemeijimeh is Gal's proposal and OpenBible's first only by its recent-trend weighting. Decided by the majority, 2026-10-19.

a6bd641.why: Arsinoe (no verse): Pleiades 727101 Clysma, alias Arsinoe (the Barrington Atlas Directory: Kum el-Qolzum/Suez), Wikidata Q3623994, Sidebotham and Mackay put it at Tall al Qulzum by Suez, 0.9 km from Pleiades' point; OpenBible's three candidates have one vote each and its resolver took the first, Ismailia on Lake Timsah, 77 km north. Decided by the majority, 2026-10-19.

aaa4c6e.why: Ramah of the Negeb (Josh 19:8; Ramoth of the Negeb of 1 Sam 30:27; Ramat-negeb of Arad ostracon 24): Tel Ira (Khirbet Gharra), where Lemaire, Na'aman and Rainey put it, and OpenBible's time-weighted first (226 to 176). Horbat Uza (Khirbet Ghazzeh), Aharoni's identification and the one most older reference works hold (6 sources to 4), was the choice of 2026-10-19; taken back 2026-10-24: ostracon 24 sends men from Arad and from Kinah to Ramat-negeb, so the two are different forts, and Horbat Uza is Kinah to OpenBible (7 sources, first by its score) and to the Biblical Archaeology Society's site list and already Kinah's point on our map. OpenBible resolved Ramah through 'another name for Baalath-beer' to Beer Yeroham, 34 km south-west. Tel Ira is also Jagur's point (OpenBible's only candidate, 14 sources, half of them rating it only possible); docs/crosswalk/their-errors.md, item 16.

a03cc2d.why: Baalath-beer (Josh 19:8, 'Baalath-beer, Ramah of the south'): one place with Ramah of the Negeb, as the verse reads and most take it; its own sites (Beer Yeroham, Tel Malhata, Tel Masos, Tel Ira) have two to four sources each. Decided by the majority, 2026-10-19; on Tel Ira with Ramah since 2026-10-24.

a14325e.why: Bealoth (Josh 15:24): another name for Baalath-beer (OpenBible's first, 16 sources); follows it.

ab049cf.why: Ramoth of the Negeb (1 Sam 30:27): another name for Ramah of the Negeb (OpenBible's only identification, 10 sources); OpenBible resolved it to Horbat Uza, it follows Ramah to Tel Ira.

a800159.why: Bealoth 2 (1 Kgs 4:16): another name for Bealoth 1 (OpenBible's only identification, 6 sources), resolved one hop to Bealoth 1's first site, Beer Yeroham (O6). Follows Bealoth 1 to Ramah's point: one place, one point, and the two Bealoths stay one dot on the map, so the place page keeps its address (/place/bealoth/).
